newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-Korean shares retreat on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-Korean shares retreat on profit taking.

text.p: Korean global depository receipts fell Tuesday on profit taking, as investors booked gains after a recent strong run, traders said.
The fall in GDRs was in line with Seoul, which also retreated. Korean shares have been in favour in past weeks due to lower interest rates and the appreciation of the yen.
There was some concern that preference share dividends could disappoint, a trader noted.
The HSBC James Capel Korea GDR Index fell 0.91 points, or 1.19 percent, to 75.11 points, a premium of 43.40 percent over the local market.
The Seoul composite index ended down 5.18 points at 769.83.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed 0.31 points up at 82.80, with the premium over the local market at 24.80 percent from 25.32 percent.
Bombay's benchmark index closed up 26.10 points at 3,861.45.
Reliance gained 12 cents to $19.75/$20.75 and Bajaj Auto lost 92 cents to $33.25/$34.75.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index fell 1.23 points, or 4.86 percent, to 120.65, representing a discount to the local market of 1.01 percent.
